item.text: Tide tables differ between ports because tides arise from the interplay of predictable astronomical forces and ref-0003 conditions that modify their timing and height. The Moon and Sun set the basic tidal frequencies, but coastline shape, underwater topography (bathymetry), and bay or estuary geometry change how tidal waves propagate and amplify. Narrow inlets and shallow shelves can increase range and delay phases, while wide continental shelves often produce smaller, slower tides. Amphidromic systems create nodes where tidal amplitude is minimal, so neighboring locations see different patterns. Weather, atmospheric pressure, and river discharge add short-term variations. Human structures—docks, breakwaters, dredging—also alter ref-0003 currents and levels. For safety, tide tables are therefore port-specific and referenced to ref-0003 datums.
